props.gloss_en: Rav Nachman: an egg [of a non-kosher bird] is nullified in sixty, and the egg is not counted
people say [of tasteless food]: like mere egg-water -- an egg gives no flavour
Abaye: here [Rav Nachman] deals with an egg containing a chick
Abaye: but a non-kosher [egg without a chick] -- no [it gives no flavour]
the baraita: kosher eggs boiled with non-kosher eggs -- if there is enough to give flavour, all are forbidden
the baraita's latter clause: eggs boiled together and a chick found in one -- if there is enough to give flavour, all are forbidden
here too [the baraita's 'non-kosher eggs'] are eggs with a chick; it calls them non-kosher because they contain a chick
Rav Asi thought to measure [the olive-bulk of fat fallen into a pot of meat] together with what the pot absorbed
Mar bar Rav Ashi thought to measure the half olive-bulk of fat in thirty half-olives
Rav Ashi: did I not tell you -- do not be lax with the measures of the Rabbis
R' Yochanan: a half-measure is forbidden by Torah law
an egg [of a non-kosher bird] in sixty is forbidden, in sixty-one permitted
R' Zeira to Rav Shemen: see that you set a limit of permission in it, for two great men of the generation did not explain the matter ... and the master resolves it
Rav Huna: an egg in sixty and it [i.e. sixty besides the egg] is forbidden
Rav Huna: in sixty-one and it, permitted
my father did not measure in forty-seven [Steinsaltz: did not require sixty, permitting at forty-seven]
Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi: and I will measure in forty-five
my father did not measure in forty-five
R' Shimon bar Rabbi: and I will measure in forty-three
R' Chiyya [to the one who came before him]: is there even thirty? [so the mixture is forbidden]
R' Chanina: [R' Chiyya's 'thirty'] was an exaggeration
all the prohibitions of the Torah are [nullified] in sixty (R' Chiyya bar Abba < RYBL < bar Kappara)
all the prohibitions of the Torah are [nullified] in a hundred (R' Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak < Rav Asi < RYBL < bar Kappara) -- set against the first report: רבי, אתה אומר כן?
and both learned it only from the cooked foreleg, as it is written: 'and the priest shall take the cooked foreleg' (Num 6:19)
the baraita: 'beshela' means only whole
RaShBY: 'beshela' means only that it was cooked with the ram
[first account] all agree it is cooked with the ram; one holds it is cut off and then cooked, the other that it is cooked and then cut off
[second account] all agree it is cut off and then cooked; but one holds it is cooked with the ram, the other in another pot
on the first account, [the derivation from the foreleg holds] according to all
on the latter account, [the derivation holds] according to RaShBY
the one who says sixty holds that we measure meat and bones against meat and bones, and it comes to sixty
the one who says a hundred holds that we measure meat against meat, and it comes to a hundred
the baraita: 'this is a permission that comes out of a prohibition' -- [the Gemara: 'this' excludes what? does it not exclude all the Torah's prohibitions?]
Abaye: [זהו] is needed only for R' Yehuda, who says a kind in its own kind is not nullified -- it teaches that here it is nullified
R' Yehuda: a kind in its own kind is not nullified
the Merciful One revealed: 'and he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat' (Lev 16:18) -- the two are together and are not nullified
[the cooked foreleg] is a novelty, and from a novelty we do not learn
do we learn [sixty or a hundred] to leniency? we learn it to stringency, for by Torah law it is nullified in a majority
Rava: [זהו] is needed only for flavour-as-substance, which in sacrifices forbids -- it teaches that here it is permitted
Rava: flavour-as-substance in sacrifices forbids

the Merciful One revealed of the sin-offering: 'whatever touches its flesh shall be holy' (Lev 6:20) -- to be like it: if it is disqualified, [what absorbed it] is disqualified, and if valid, it is eaten by its stricter rules
Ravina: [זהו] is needed only for the place of the cut, which elsewhere is forbidden and here permitted
as was said: the place of the cut is elsewhere forbidden
the mishna (Orla 2:6): why did they say of whatever leavens, flavours or mixes teruma -- to stringency in a kind with its kind, to leniency and stringency in a kind not of its kind
the seifa (Orla 2:7): split beans cooked with lentils -- if they give flavour, forbidden whether or not there is enough to raise them in a hundred and one
if they do not give flavour, permitted whether or not there is enough to raise them in a hundred and one
the reisha: wheat leaven fallen into wheat dough, enough to leaven -- forbidden whether or not there is enough to raise it in a hundred and one
not enough to raise it in a hundred and one -- forbidden whether or not it can leaven
Rav Dimi: no -- [the seifa's 'not enough for a hundred and one' means] in a hundred
Rav Dimi: no -- the reisha is in a hundred and one, and the seifa in a hundred
Abaye: perhaps leaven is different, for its leavening is strong
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: not all the measures are equal, for brine's measure is close to two hundred
the mishna (Terumot 10:8): the brine of a non-kosher fish is forbidden
R' Yehuda: a revi'it [of the brine forbids] in two se'a
brine is different, for it is mere sweat
